__NOTOC__ {{recipesummary | Category = Puerto Rican recipes | Time = 5 hours | Difficulty = 3 | Level = 4 }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Puerto Rico|Cuisine of Puerto Rico]] This recipe for '''pavo relleno de mofongo''' was submitted by Brenda Ortiz Valle, who said the following:
"This recipe is my mom's, Aida E Valle, special Turkey recipe. The best I have tasted in my life!!"
==Ingredients== === Filling === * 3 medium to large green [[Cookbook:Plantain|plantains]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Canola Oil|canola oil]] * 1 large [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomato]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]] * 1 red [[Cookbook:Bell Pepper|bell pepper]], cut into ½-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] squares * 1 green bell pepper, cut into ½-inch squares * 2 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] * ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] [[Cookbook:Adobo Sauce|adobo]] === Turkey === * ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] * ¼ cup [[Cookbook:Wine vinegar|red wine vinegar]] * 2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]] adobo * 2 tbsp [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]] * 1 tbsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * 1 tbsp of ground [[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] * 2 packages of ground "cubitos" (Cubitos en polvo—[[Cookbook:Bouillon Cube|chicken bouillon cubes]]) * 2 packages of uncolored sazon (sazon sin achiote—uncolored seasoned salt. Goya is a typical brand.) * 4 large cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] * 1 whole [[Cookbook:Turkey|turkey]] (15 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]]) ==Procedure== === Filling === # Peel plantains and [[Cookbook:Slicing|slice]] into 1-inch chunks. # Add 2 cups canola oil to a medium-size [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|frying pan]]. Set stove to medium-high and heat the frying pan for about 5 minutes. # Add plantains and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] until they are golden brown. Drain them on [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]] or brown paper bags. # Squash plantains one-by-one using a [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|mortar]], and place into a medium size bowl. # Add, tomato, red and green pepper, garlic, olive oil, and adobo to the bowl containing the squashed plantains, then mix. === Turkey === # In a small bowl mix olive oil, red wine vinegar, adobo, oregano, salt, ground pepper, "cubitos", "sazon", and garlic. # With a sharp knife, make incisions in different places of the turkey. # Use seasoning mixture to season whole turkey, inside and out. If you need more seasoning mix, repeat first step. # Cover turkey with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]] and refrigerate until it absorbs the seasoning, at least 2–4 hours, preferably overnight. # Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 350°F (175°C). # Fill turkey with plantain filling. Cover, the turkey filling opening with kitchen thread.Alton Brown shows how to truss a turkey here: http://www.foodnetwork.com/videos/how-to-truss-a-turkey/27751.html #Cover turkey with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]] and place turkey in preheated oven. #Leave turkey within the first 2 hours without removing aluminum foil. After 2 hours, remove aluminum foil and turn in ½ hour intervals for two hours. Use the turkey drippings to moist turkey while cooking. #Set oven to [[Cookbook:Broiling|broil]] for 20 minutes each side. == Notes, tips, and variations == [[Category:Puerto Rican recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using turkey]] [[Category:Gluten-free recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using banana]] [[Category:Recipes for stuffing and dressing]] [[Category:Main course recipes]] [[Category:Roasted recipes]] [[Category:Family heritage recipes]] [[Category:Recipes using red bell pepper]] [[Category:Recipes using green bell pepper]] [[Category:Recipes using garlic]] [[Category:Recipes using canola oil]]

steps.text: Peel plantains and slice into 1-inch chunks.
Add 2 cups canola oil to a medium-size frying pan. Set stove to medium-high and heat the frying pan for about 5 minutes.
Add plantains and fry until they are golden brown. Drain them on paper towels or brown paper bags.
Squash plantains one-by-one using a mortar, and place into a medium size bowl.
Add, tomato, red and green pepper, garlic, olive oil, and adobo to the bowl containing the squashed plantains, then mix.
In a small bowl mix olive oil, red wine vinegar, adobo, oregano, salt, ground pepper, "cubitos", "sazon", and garlic.
With a sharp knife, make incisions in different places of the turkey.
Use seasoning mixture to season whole turkey, inside and out. If you need more seasoning mix, repeat first step.
Cover turkey with aluminum foil and refrigerate until it absorbs the seasoning, at least 2–4 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).

Fill turkey with plantain filling. Cover, the turkey filling opening with kitchen thread.Alton Brown shows how to truss a turkey here: http://www.foodnetwork.com/videos/how-to-truss-a-turkey/27751.html
Cover turkey with aluminum foil and place turkey in preheated oven.

Leave turkey within the first 2 hours without removing aluminum foil. After 2 hours, remove aluminum foil and turn in ½ hour intervals for two hours. Use the turkey drippings to moist turkey while cooking.
Set oven to broil for 20 minutes each side.
